text:
alex: Quick follow-up on the soft-throttle handshake RFC — we need to pick the demotion semantics + telemetry surface before we prod-roll. thoughts?

sam: Are we still leaning toward a two-tier demotion (soft -> hard) or immediate hard for severe abuse? I worry about client-visible flapping. :thinking_face:

priya: vote for two-tier. soft should mean degraded QPS with preserved latency SLO for small reqs, hard means full reject. soft must expose a clear header so SDKs can backoff gracefully.

miguel: agree with priya. also: we must tag metrics with "throttle_cause=[fairness|abuse|capacity]" so ops can filter. otherwise dashboards are useless.

jess: on abuse signals — do we unify scoring in the quota-coordinator or keep a fast local heuristic? central gives consistency, local gives speed. tradeoff: false positives in local heuristics cause customer pain.

priya: proposal: local heuristic for immediate short windows (100ms-5s) with central reconciliation every 30s. local action = soft demotion only. central can escalate to hard after aggregation. reduces latency of reaction but keeps final authority centralized.

alex: that matches what we discussed in infra-ORCH doc but we need telemetry to prove it doesn't over-demote. what metrics/labels we need?

miguel: minimum: tenant_id, route, decision={allow,soft_demote,hard_reject}, reason_tag, local_vs_central, window_ms, token_balance_before. also sample a few request traces for postmortem.

jess: add abuse_score snapshot (top signals) when decision!=allow. i.e. "abuse_signals=[rapid_repeats,high_token_cost,anon_proxy]". keep sampled payloads out of logs but link to trace id.

infra-bot: Deployment note: canary config will be applied to 10% of ingress pods. Metric pipeline: new labels will be available under telemetry.v2 in ~2h after deploy.

sam: config sketch — putting this here so it's easy to test locally: 

```
throttle_policy:
  local_heuristic:
    window_ms: 2000
    burst_threshold: 3
    action: soft_demote
  central_reconcile:
    reconcile_interval_s: 30
    escalate_after_hits: 5
    action: hard_reject
  headers:
    soft_demote: X-Redwood-Soft-Demotion: true
```

priya: small experiment idea: for canary tenants toggle local_heuristic on/off and compare 95p latency + soft_demote rate. rollout plan: 10% pods -> 10 tenants -> 50 tenants. measure for 48h between steps.

miguel: telemetry notes: Prom query for demo: 
```
sum by (tenant_id, decision, reason_tag) (increase(inference_throttle_decisions_total[1h]))
```
That should highlight hot tenants and predominant reasons.

jess: edge case: multi-tenant multiplexed connections (same TCP) — local heuristics could misattribute bursts. We need to ensure connection-level counters are split by tenant metadata before local decisions.

alex: good catch. infra task: ensure metadata extraction hook runs before local heuristic. @miguel can you own that?

miguel: yep will add extraction to prefilter stage. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: one more: what about fairness scheduling interaction? if we soft-demote a tenant, scheduler should reduce batch weight gracefully not just drop them to lower priority queue. else we create latency cliffs for others.

priya: scheduler change proposed: when tenant in soft_demote, multiply batch_weight by 0.5 and set admission_retry_delay += 50ms. Hard_reject bypasses scheduler (immediate 429).

jess: add a circuit breaker for tenants that oscillate between demote and allow rapidly — escalate window counts to avoid thrashing.

alex: action items:
- miguel: add metadata extraction to prefilter + telemetry labels (owner) — due TOMORROW EOD
- priya: write canary experiment runbook + success criteria (latency delta, demote rate) — due Fri COB
- sam: implement scheduler weight multiplier + retry delay hooks (prototype) — due next Wed
- jess: finalize abuse signal list and sampling policy — due Fri
- infra-bot: schedule canary rollout when above are ready

sam: acked. I'll prototype weight multiplier in the scheduler repo and post a small PR.

miguel: infra note: expect ~200 new metrics series initially because of extra labels. quota telemetry shard might need a small bump. raising with infra-sre.

jess: non-blocking question: should SDKs surface X-Redwood-Soft-Demotion automatically to downstream app logs or leave to user? my vote: SDK logs at debug by default and provide opt-in hook.

priya: opt-in is safest. lots of customers will treat any header as an error today.

alex: agreed opt-in. final ask: keep the RFC doc updated with demotion examples and a short FAQ for support. I'll capture the runbook and PR pointers in the RFC patch.

infra-bot: noted. Next sync in 48h unless issues emerge.

sam: :+1:

miguel: :eyes:

jess: thanks everyone, i'll start sampling rules and share a draft.
